sentences.text: Elanodactylus is a pterosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous period found in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
The holotype specimen — the single fossil the species is based on — preserves a partial skeleton including wings, sternum, shoulder girdle, ribs, and neck and back vertebrae but lacks the skull.
This animal possesses a unique trait where the first finger bone is shorter than the second and third finger bones.
The holotype had a wingspan of about 2.5 meters and an estimated weight of 10 kilograms.
The species name prolatus means "elongated" in Latin, referring to the animal's elongated middle neck vertebrae.
The genus Elanodactylus was named in 2008 by paleontologists Brian Andres and Ji Qiang.
The name Elanodactylus combines the kite genus Elanus for its long wings and the Greek word daktylos for the wing finger.
The neck vertebrae of Elanodactylus have exapophyses, a feature similar to the giant Late Cretaceous pterosaurs known as azhdarchids.
A 2018 phylogenetic analysis placed Elanodactylus within the family Ctenochasmatidae.
Elanodactylus belongs to the family Ctenochasmatidae.
Elanodactylus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Researchers suggest that Elanodactylus is a ctenochasmatid and that its neck vertebrae evolved convergently with those of azhdarchids.
